name: Mesoeye

lead: Mesoeye is a name for under-eye mesotherapy, a clinic treatment of tiny injections around the eyes. People use it hoping for brighter, less tired-looking skin there.
Sessions are done by a practitioner and usually repeated.

paras: A preparation is placed in the superficial skin of the eye area to hydrate and nourish it.
Bruising, swelling, redness and, with poor hygiene, infection are reported for mesotherapy. In the US, injected mixtures are overseen by state medical boards rather than FDA.

angle.text: Mesoeye is used as a clinic procedure aimed at brighter, more hydrated under-eye skin. Sessions are typically repeated over several visits.

lead: Mesoeye is a name used for under-eye mesotherapy, a cosmetic procedure in which a practitioner places small superficial injections of a nourishing or brightening preparation into the thin skin around the eyes. People seek it to soften the look of dark circles and tired-looking eye contours for a fresher face.

Mesotherapy in general is a technique of intradermal or subcutaneous injection of vitamins, plant extracts, hyaluronic acid and similar substances, with the stated aim of hydrating and nourishing the skin.[1]
infobox: Practitioners regulated by state medical boards (US)[1]

paras: Cosmetic mesotherapy was founded by Michel Pistor, and the French press coined the term in 1958; France recognized it as a medical specialty in 1987.[1] A needle-free pressurized variant also exists.[1]

Reported mesotherapy reactions include bruising, swelling, pain and redness.[1] Infections have been documented after procedures done under unhygienic conditions, and French investigators traced adverse effects to hygiene rather than the treatment itself.[1]

No studies found. Related: a small study of four facial multivitamin mesotherapy sessions in 10 patients found no clinically relevant skin rejuvenation, and cosmetic mesotherapy overall has generally not been tested in standard clinical trials.[1]

timeline.event: The French press coins the term mesotherapy.[1]
